summary: ASTRA is an offline-first astronaut wellness and health-tracking companion designed for deep-space missions like Artemis and Mars transit. When Earth is up to 22 minutes away by radio, real-time medical guidance is impossible. ASTRA continuously evaluates everyday biometric check-ins against the astronaut’s personal mission baseline rather than rigid Earth averages. It maps health shifts directly to NASA’s Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight, surfaces actionable, non-diagnostic recovery steps, and exports timestamped clinical logs for flight surgeons—all running locally inside the spacecraft cabin with zero server or internet reliance.
details:
What it does & How it works:

ASTRA (Astronaut Space-health Tracking, Risk insights & Assistance) is an offline-first astronaut wellness dashboard designed for long-duration deep-space exploration (Artemis, Mars transit). Astronauts take a 2-minute daily check-in logging core vitals (heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, SpO₂), operational biomarkers (sleep hours, subjective mood, stress score, hydration, and exercise), and physical symptoms.

ASTRA analyzes these inputs using a transparent, deterministic rule-based engine that compares readings against two reference layers: clinical spaceflight thresholds (informed by NASA-STD-3001) and the astronaut's rolling personal baseline (the mean of their previous 10 check-ins, flagging shifts exceeding ±2 standard deviations). When an anomaly or multi-day trend (such as 3 consecutive days of poor sleep and rising resting heart rate) is detected, ASTRA generates an explainable alert linking the observation to one of NASA’s Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight (Radiation, Isolation, Distance from Earth, Gravity fields, or Hostile/Closed Environments). It offers non-diagnostic next steps, logs crew countermeasures, and formats a standardized crew-to-ground health summary exportable as a secure JSON/CSV file for Earth-based flight surgeons.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Communication delays on Mars missions reach up to 22 minutes each way, eliminating immediate telemedicine. ASTRA empowers crew self-reliance by identifying subclinical health drifts before they evolve into medical emergencies. It reduces cognitive fatigue and provides structured, objective data for flight surgeons once transmission windows open. Beyond spaceflight, ASTRA’s zero-network architecture directly benefits isolated Earth populations: Antarctic research stations, naval submarines, and remote rural clinics.

Tools, Languages, & Software Used:

- Frontend & Architecture: React 19, TypeScript, TanStack Start, Vite

- Styling & Components: Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui design tokens, Lucide React icons

- Data Visualization: Recharts (trend graphs and baseline tracking)

- Testing & Quality: Vitest (unit tests validating anomaly and baseline evaluation logic)

- Storage: Browser-local storage (ensuring 100% offline functionality without external server dependencies)

Creativity & Factors Considered:

1. Spaceflight-Specific Ergonomics: A dark, low-glare UI optimized for cabin lighting and high contrast under fatigue.

2. Ethical Guardrails & NASA Safety Guidelines: ASTRA strictly avoids black-box algorithmic diagnosis. Every alert clearly identifies its limitation, frames recommendations as self-care protocols, and instructs the astronaut when to log ground communications.

3. Offline Autonomy: Zero cloud dependencies ensure uninterrupted reliability in deep space with no telemetry lock.
